newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines rejects Taiwan APEC upgrade bid.
newsitem.headline: Philippines rejects Taiwan APEC upgrade bid.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday firmly rejected a bid by Taiwan to upgrade its participation in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit to be held in the Philippines next month.

Ramos said APEC leaders had agreed that Taiwan's representation would be decided by consensus, and in previous APEC summits the consensus was that Taipei should be represented by its economic minister or someone of equivalent rank.
"That is the agreed approach and that still stands and so while we receive and consider all of these appeals we have no recourse but to use the agreed formula," he told his weekly news conference.
Diplomatic sources said Taiwan had submitted the name of Vice President Lien Chan as its representative in the APEC summit to be held at the Subic free port near Manila on November 25.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war separated them in 1949, said on Tuesday it would not accept any plans to upgrade Taiwan's representation.
"The Chinese side will definitely not accept any practice that goes beyond this formula," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.
A Taiwan newspaper recently reported that Manila had promised to allow either Lien or Taiwan Vice Premier Hsu Li-teh to attend the summit.
"Do not believe everything you read in the newspapers," Ramos said.
